primary.method: single change point, exhaustive least-squares split

sensitivity.name: variable
sensitivity.change: locate the boundary on percent_correct instead of angle error

sensitivity.name: level
sensitivity.change: run the primary analysis at session level (n=11) as well as block level (n=21)

reversibility_tests.name: T5 excursion
reversibility_tests.success_criterion: indicator at day 2149 returns to within the range spanned by days 2121-2128
reversibility_tests.failure_criterion: indicator at day 2149 remains at or above its degraded-period level, indicating the measure tracks elapsed time or accumulated drift rather than system dynamics

reversibility_tests.name: T11 internal excursion
reversibility_tests.success_criterion: indicator at day 751 returns to within the range spanned by days 658-675

secondary_outcome_neural_vs_behavioural.question: does the neural indicator warn earlier than simply watching performance?
secondary_outcome_neural_vs_behavioural.rationale: predicting a collapse that was already visible in behaviour is worth little; warning before behaviour shows anything is worth a great deal
secondary_outcome_neural_vs_behavioural.baseline_blocks: first 8 T11 blocks (trial days 658-675), which precede every candidate destabilization date
secondary_outcome_neural_vs_behavioural.detection_rule: first block exceeding baseline mean + k*SD and staying beyond it for p consecutive blocks
secondary_outcome_neural_vs_behavioural.outcome: detection_day(behaviour) - detection_day(neural), in trial days; positive means the neural indicator warned first
secondary_outcome_neural_vs_behavioural.why_a_grid: the rule is known to be parameter-sensitive (the destabilization date moves 26 days across this grid), so the full distribution is reported rather than one setting; both signals use identical parameters at every setting, which keeps the COMPARISON fair even though either date alone is not well determined

interpretation_fixed_in_advance.lead_positive_majority: neural monitoring detects earlier than behavioural monitoring
interpretation_fixed_in_advance.lead_negative: behaviour detects first; the neural indicator adds nothing and will be reported as such

rejected_because: the destabilization IS the early-warning signal; making it the event would require a new warning before it, and the period before day 689 is flat and healthy
its date is not determined: across 24 parameter combinations the onset lands on day 689 (12/24), day 715 (10/24) or day 709 (2/24) — a 26-day spread
per-session tests sit exactly at the smallest p-value the sample size allows (0.0444), so they carry no information about effect size
it costs most of the sample: 8 blocks before day 689 or 16 before day 715, against 21 before day 758
destabilization_as_the_event.retained_as: a comparator in the secondary outcome above

statistics.two_sided_rationale: a compressed basin can produce falling indicators before a transition (Titus et al. 2019), so a one-sided test would miss real signals

power_statement.commitment: a null result will be reported as a null, not reworked until something appears

still_open_after_freezing: which neural observable carries the indicator (raw 20 ms features are ruled out: near-white, 0.3-0.5 bins of memory)
rolling-window length, which must be swept and reported as a surface

declaration: This design was fixed before any early-warning indicator was computed on the real data. The deterioration boundary was located from behavioural performance only. No EWS result was known at the time of freezing.
